team.summary: Four founders with fintech and blockchain background; YC W25 batch; team of 9.
team.technicalDepth: [inferred] Building a stablecoin payment API requires deep blockchain, cryptography, and financial infrastructure expertise.

market.sizeHint: [inferred] Global cross-border payments market is trillions of dollars; stablecoin settlement volume growing rapidly.
market.competitiveLandscape: [inferred] Competitors include Circle (USDC), Stripe (crypto), Bridge, and other stablecoin payment APIs.
market.whyNow: [inferred] Stablecoin adoption accelerating due to regulatory clarity, lower transaction costs, and demand for instant global settlement.

risks.text: Regulatory uncertainty around stablecoins and money transmission licenses across jurisdictions
Dependence on third-party stablecoin issuers (e.g., Circle, Tether) and blockchain networks
Competition from well-funded incumbents (Stripe, Circle) and other crypto payment startups
Technical complexity of maintaining multi-chain, multi-currency infrastructure

subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Four technical founders with apparent fintech/blockchain domain fit; YC W25 acceptance signals strong founder quality; team of 9 indicates early execution capacity. Prior exits unknown.

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: Potential workflow lock-in via API integration and multi-chain abstraction; switching costs moderate once developers embed the API. No proprietary data moat yet. Dependence on external stablecoin issuers and blockchains limits vertical control.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: Not an AI-native agent; it's a traditional API product. Self-serve onboarding for developers likely. Clear one-sentence value prop. Scores low on AI-agent criterion but meets other product criteria.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: Specific vertical (stablecoin payments) with massive TAM. Strong why-now: stablecoin adoption inflection, regulatory progress, developer demand for programmable money. Clear competitors and wedge (developer-first API).

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: YC W25 batch (very recent) is a strong fresh signal. Team size 9 suggests post-formation momentum. No public data on paying customers, revenue, or active usage yet.

scoreRationale: BlindPay shows strong team and market timing with a clear wedge in stablecoin payments. Defensibility is moderate due to reliance on external protocols. Product is not AI-native, which lowers its score per the rubric's AI-agent emphasis. Traction is early but fresh with YC acceptance. Overall, a promising early-stage fintech infrastructure play.
